children: , the semiconductor designer and manufacturer rebuilding its foundry operation, extended its rally by approximately 1.6% to $106.075 Wednesday after surging 9.1% Tuesday. Northland upgraded the stock from Market Perform to Outperform and set a $120 price target, adding fresh momentum to Intel's turnaround story.

The operating numbers are finally moving in the right direction. Intel's second-quarter results showed revenue rising 25% to $16.1 billion, while Data Center and AI sales rocketed 59% to $6.3 billion. GAAP gross margin expanded 12.9 percentage points to 40.4%, and operating margin rebounded to 11.1% from a loss a year earlier.

Data Center and AI now generates roughly 39% of total revenue, but the valuation leaves little room for a stumble. The picture shows Intel trading 231.8% above its GF Value estimate of $31.97, while Northland's $120 target offers only about 13% upside from $106.075. The turnaround is gaining muscle, but Intel still must defend server pricing, secure outside foundry customers and convert heavy investment into durable cash flow.

title: Intel Rises After a $120 Target Meets 59% AI Growth
